name: com.sulihuli/catalog
title: SuliHuli EV catalog
description: Electric-vehicle specs, prices, rankings and comparisons; every figure with its source and date.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Find any SuliHuli page by words: editorial answers to EV questions, guides (running cost, winter range, upcoming EVs, value map, cheat sheet), rankings, brands, incentives per country, models, the ranking method, sources, legal and trust pages. Use it for questions a page answers, e.g. 'which EVs have a third row' or 'how long to install a home charger'; read a result whole with fetch. Returns id, title, url, kind and a short excerpt per page. For numbers, filters and rankings of models use search_models.

query.description: Words of the question or the page, any order, e.g. 'home charger install time', 'germany grant', 'methodology'.

kind.description: Optional: only pages of this kind.

locale.description: Language of the answer's text and page links (default en): en.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: One SuliHuli page in full as Markdown, the same text as its .md address: an answer, a guide, a ranking, a brand, a model or its sources and charging pages, incentives, the method or a legal page. Use it after search, or with any SuliHuli address you have. Long pages come in parts of up to 8 000 characters including navigation: the first part includes a contents list with part numbers; pass part for the next. Quote figures with the source and status the page prints.

id.description: The id from search, or any SuliHuli address: a path such as '/answers/how-long-to-install-home-ev-charger' or '/m/kia-ev9/sources', or the full URL.

part.description: Part of a long page, 1-based (default 1); see total_parts.

locale.description: Language of the answer's text and page links (default en): en.

tools.name: search_models
tools.description: Find electric vehicles by brand or model name, or list the whole catalog ranked for a use case, optionally only those with at least a given range. Use it first whenever you have a name but no slug, and for questions like 'which EVs go furthest' or 'best family EV'. Returns per model the slug (pass it to get_model or compare_models), score out of 100 (SuliHuli Index 4.4 by default, or the use-case score of another preset), official range with its test cycle and the WLTP-equivalent, DC 10-80 % minutes, battery kWh, which of them are unverified, markets and the page URL. A minimum range is compared on the basis named in range_basis, and the answer says which. There is no price or market filter: read prices per market with get_model. Paged: total, page, total_pages. detail 'full' adds each figure's source and the cover photo credit.

query.description: Words of the brand and/or model name, any order, case-insensitive; every word must match, e.g. 'tesla 3', 'ioniq', 'bmw ix'. Omit to rank the whole catalog.

preset.description: What the ranking optimizes for (default index): index (the main score: passport 40 %, people 30 %, market 30 %); everyday (a balanced daily driver — range, charging and practicality); long_range (maximum distance per charge for road trips); family (space, seats and practicality for a family); performance (acceleration and fast-charging capability); city (a short, easy-to-park car that still charges fast); winter (range that survives the cold — ranked on our own winter estimate).

min_range_km.description: Only EVs whose range is at least this many kilometres, on the basis of range_basis. For miles, multiply by 1.609: 300 miles = 483 km.

range_basis.description: What min_range_km is compared with: wltp_equivalent (default; an EPA figure x1.15, CLTC x0.82, NEDC x0.80), official (the published figure on its own cycle), or one cycle - epa, wltp, cltc, nedc - whose own figure must reach it (a model without a figure on that cycle is left out). A US '300 miles' is an EPA figure: range_basis 'epa'.

limit.description: Models per page (default 20, at most 50 without an API key).

page.description: Page number, 1-based (default 1); see total_pages in the answer.

detail.description: summary (default): the short answer. full: every row as well, with source chains and photo credits.

locale.description: Language of the answer's text and page links (default en): en.

tools.name: get_model
tools.description: Everything SuliHuli holds on one electric vehicle: range per test cycle (WLTP, EPA, CLTC, NEDC), charging, efficiency, battery and the other specs, prices per market and version with their dates, and every figure's source link, date and status (verified or unverified; where sources disagree, each figure is shown with its source, never averaged). The headline figures describe one named version; the answer names every version we know. For another version pass `version` (name words such as 'long range awd', or a key from the list) and get that version's own figures. Short by default: the headline figures, the named version's price per market and the version names; `sections` gives any part whole (every figure, every price row, each version's summary, the full Markdown page with photo credits). Use it to answer any question about a specific model, quoting the figure with its cycle, source and status.

slug.description: Model slug as search_models returns it (also the last part of the page URL https://sulihuli.com/m/<slug>), e.g. 'hyundai-ioniq-6'. A version slug such as 'tesla-model-y-long-range-awd' also works.

version.description: Optional: a version key or name words, e.g. 'long range awd'. Without it the answer describes the named version and lists the others.

sections.description: Optional parts to give whole: figures (every figure with its source), prices (every price row of every market and version, in pages of 40), versions (each version's sourced figures), page (the full Markdown page as text). Without it the answer is short. Parts that would pass 40 000 characters together are named in sections_left for another call.

prices_page.description: Page of the full price list with sections ['prices'] (default 1); see prices_pages.

locale.description: Language of the answer's text and page links (default en): en.

tools.name: compare_models
tools.description: Side-by-side comparison of two to four electric vehicles: range (each with its test cycle), charging, battery, price and the other specs, the leading value marked per row, a short verdict, the version each column stands for, sources and cover photo credits. Each model is compared on its named version, and every figure says which version it belongs to. Use it for 'X vs Y' and 'which should I buy' questions; get slugs from search_models first. Pass `slugs`, or `slug_a` and `slug_b`. Returns Markdown with the canonical comparison URL, plus the figures and each named version's price per market as structured fields; detail 'full' adds every price row.

slugs.description: Two to four model slugs, e.g. ['tesla-model-3', 'hyundai-ioniq-6'].

slug_a.description: Shorter two-model form: first model slug (use with slug_b instead of slugs).

detail.description: summary (default): the short answer. full: every row as well, with source chains and photo credits.

locale.description: Language of the answer's text and page links (default en): en.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: The published 'best EV for ...' rankings (everyday, long range, long range over 500 km, family, performance): slug, title, the preset each ranks by and what it optimizes for, and the page URL. Use it to pick a ranking, then open it with get_category_ranking. Returns JSON.

locale.description: Language of the answer's text and page links (default en): en.

tools.name: get_category_ranking
tools.description: One 'best EV for ...' ranking: the top 25 models in order with score out of 100, published range with its test cycle, DC charging 10-80 % time and battery (unverified figures marked with their source), the public ranking method, and links to each model. Use it for 'what are the best EVs for ...' questions; take the slug from list_categories and quote the criterion with the list. Returns Markdown with the canonical page URL, plus the ranked rows as structured fields.

locale.description: Language of the answer's text and page links (default en): en.

tools.name: get_incentives
tools.description: Grants, tax credits and subsidies for buying an electric car in one country: each open program's amount, price cap, who pays, end date, official source and the date we checked it; ended programs named. Use it for questions like 'what EV grant is there in Germany'. Without market: every market we track with its summary. detail 'full' adds eligibility and the ended programs' details.

market.description: Two-letter market code. Omit to list the markets.

detail.description: summary (default): the short answer. full: every row as well, with source chains and photo credits.

locale.description: Language of the answer's text and page links (default en): en.

tools.name: get_ownership_cost
tools.description: What an electric car costs to run and own: energy cost per 100 km, per year and over the years, plus the comparable new price and the total, in USD. Use it for 'what does an Ioniq 6 cost to run per year' (pass slug and your annual_km) or 'cheapest EV to own over 5 years' (no slug: a ranking). Every figure is an estimate from the model's consumption and an illustrative tariff you can replace; the answer names the price row and what is excluded.

slug.description: Model slug as search_models returns it (also the last part of the page URL https://sulihuli.com/m/<slug>), e.g. 'hyundai-ioniq-6'. Omit to rank the cheapest to own.

market.description: Two-letter purchase market, e.g. GB or DE. Omit to use the card price for a model or US prices for the ranking. Electricity tariff is separate.

annual_km.description: Kilometres a year (default 15000). For miles, multiply by 1.609.

tariff_usd_per_kwh.description: Electricity price in USD per kWh (default 0.19, an illustrative home tariff).

limit.description: Without slug: models in the ranking (default 10).

locale.description: Language of the answer's text and page links (default en): en.

tools.name: get_changes
tools.description: Find upcoming EV launches and observed catalog price changes since a date. Use it for 'what EVs are launching or have changed price since November 1?'. Launches follow /upcoming and can be in the future. Year or month dates qualify when the period starts on or after since. Prices compare dated observations for the same version, market, currency, price type, basis and source. The newer observation dates the change. An empty list means no matching catalog records.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1 (default). 10 events per page.

locale.description: Language of the answer's text and page links (default en): en.
